To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(i) the fatty acid composition influences the binding and internalization (uptake) of chylomicrons by hepatocytes from animals fed a low-fat (LF) or a high-fat (HF) diet, and (ii) the effects are mediated by the LDL receptor and/or the LDL receptor-related (LRP) protein.
the fatty acid composition influences the binding and uptake of chylmicron remnants by hepatocytes, and that the LDL receptor plays a major role in this process.

the fatty acid composition (and hence the degree of unsaturation) of chylomicrons and chylomicron remnant particles influences their hepatic binding and internalization, but that the mechanism of these effects is different when hepatocytes from normal rats are used compared to those from animals fed a diet enriched in fat.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the role of dietary fats in the pathogenesis of atherosclerosis.
the influence of the fatty acid composition on the binding and internalization process.
the influence of fatty acids and their metabolites on the metabolism of lipoproteins and their components in the liver.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
, in the rat, the fatty acid composition affects the binding and internalization processes in the liver.

the fatty acid composition and/or the fatty acid content of chylomicrons and chylomicron-remnants influence the rate of their hepatic uptake, and that the LDL receptor and LRP are involved in this process.
the fatty acid composition and the amount of dietary fat affect the hepatic uptake and metabolism of chylomicrons and chylomicron remnant lipoproteins.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the uptake of chylomicon remnants is influenced by the composition of the remnants themselves and also by longer-term adaptive effects in the liver, and that these effects may involve both the low-density lipoproteins receptor (LDL receptor) and the LDL receptor-related receptor (LRP).

the fatty acid composition and the dietary source of chylomicrons and their remnants influence their uptake by hepatocytes and that these effects are due to the fatty acids themselves rather than to the presence of different dietary lipids.
the fatty acid composition and the dietary intake influence the binding and internalization processes of chylomicrons and chylomicron remnant in the liver.
The main takeaway from our work is that
dietary fatty acids can have an important influence on the hepatic uptake and metabolism of dietary lipoproteins.
the fatty acid composition and the amount of fat consumed influence the hepatic uptake and metabolism of lipoproteins.
the fatty acid composition influences chylomicron remnant binding and internalization, but this effect is modified by the diet.
